title: I didn't ... Did you ... ? (past simple negative and questions)
subtitle: I didn't go / Did you go?
summary: Make past simple negatives with didn't and past simple questions with did, always followed by the simple verb.

lesson.heading: did in negatives and questions
lesson.text: In the past simple we use **did** to make negatives and questions. The main verb goes back to its simple form: **play**, **watch**, **have**, **go**.

examples.text: I **played** tennis yesterday, but I **didn't win**.
'**Did** you **do** the shopping?' 'No, I **didn't have** time.'
We **went** to the cinema, but we **didn't enjoy** the film.

lesson.heading: did/didn't + simple verb
lesson.text: After **did** and **didn't** the verb never has a past form and never has -ed. Compare: I **watched** -> I **didn't watch**; they **went** -> **did** they **go**?; he **had** -> he **didn't have**.

lesson.heading: Short answers
rows: Yes, I / we / you / they did.
No, I / we / you / they didn't.
lesson.note: 'Did it rain on Sunday?' 'Yes, it did.' - 'Did Helen come to the party?' 'No, she didn't.'

lesson.text: One past form is enough: it sits on **did/didn't**, so the main verb stays simple - *I didn't go*, *Did you go?*

exercises.prompt: I saw Barbara, but I ___ Jane.
exercises.explanation: After didn't the verb is simple: didn't see (not didn't saw).

exercises.prompt: They worked on Monday, but they ___ on Tuesday.
You say: 'I enjoyed the party. How about you?' How do you ask the question?
exercises.explanation: did + subject + simple verb: Did you enjoy ... ?

exercises.prompt: A tells B some news. Match A's sentence with B's question.

pairs.left: We went to New York last month.

pairs.right: Did you go to bed late?

pairs.left: We went to the beach yesterday.
pairs.right: Did you have a nice time?

exercises.prompt: You say: 'I had a good holiday. How about you?' Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: Did you have a good holiday?

exercises.statement: Did you sleep well last night?
exercises.explanation: Correct. did + subject + the simple verb sleep.

exercises.prompt: She had a pen, but she ___ any paper.
exercises.explanation: had becomes didn't have in the negative.

exercises.prompt: Does the gap need the past simple form of the verb, or didn't + the simple verb?

items.text: We were tired, so we ___ long at the party. (not stay)
It was very warm in the room, so I ___ a window. (open)
'Did you phone Chris?' 'No, I ___ time.' (not have)

exercises.statement: We went to the cinema, but we didn't enjoyed the film.
exercises.explanation: We didn't enjoy the film. After didn't the verb has no -ed.

exercises.prompt: *A:* ___ yesterday? *B:* No, it was a nice day.
*A:* I was late for the meeting. *B:* What time ___ ? *A:* Half past nine.
exercises.explanation: Question word + did + subject + simple verb.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Why weren't you at the meeting yesterday? *B:* I ___ about it.
exercises.explanation: knew becomes didn't know in the negative.
